at-0001.title: Round money only with round_money
at-0001.content: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

at-0002.title: Coerce amounts with to_money and ZERO
at-0002.content: Wrap raw Decimal amounts with ledgerly.money.to_money and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO, as line_total and invoice_total do, so arithmetic stays consistent across the money module.

at-0003.title: Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes
at-0003.content: Reject invalid input in ledgerly/invoice.py by raising BillingError(code, detail) with snake_case codes such as "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount"; reuse the same code for the same condition across functions (e.g. issue_invoice also uses "invalid_state").

at-0004.title: Reject bools when validating integer quantities
at-0004.content: When validating integer fields like quantity, explicitly exclude bool via isinstance(quantity, bool) before the int check, since True/False are ints in Python.

at-0005.content: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
